content.text: ▪︎common condition affecting the oral + genital mucosa
▪︎⍉known cause, may be assoc w/ HHV-6
▪︎IBD, celiac dz, SLE, B12/folate deficiency, HIV, MTX
▪︎also assoc: genetic predisposition, immunosuppression, poor oral hygiene, food allergies, + stress
▪︎simple aphthosis = MC form; sporadic episodes throughout the yr, limited to the oral mucosa; ulcers typically 3-5 mm + heal w/in 1-2 wks
▪︎complex aphthosis = oral + genital mucosa ulcers; typically >1 cm, more painful than simple, + can take up to 6 wks to heal; USU ≥1 active ulcer
▪︎ulcer morphology: minor, major, or herpetiform; herpetiform = 1-2 mm each in clusters, may coalesce into larger ulcers
▪︎recurrent oral + genital ulcers → evaluate for Behçet syndrome
▪︎often triggered by minimal trauma (ex, biting the tongue)
▪︎appear on nonkeratinized mucosa (buccal + lip mucosa); rarely labia minora (Lipschütz ulcer)
▪︎pain mgmt: 2% viscous lidocaine, diphenhydramine liquid, or dyclonine lozenges
▪︎2° infection w/ Candida or bacteria → clotrimazole troches, nystatin suspensions, or chlorhexidine mouth rinses
▪︎dexamethasone elixir = 1st-line for simple stomatitis; most effective if started at sx onset
▪︎complex stomatitis unresponsive to topical therapies → oral prednisone x4-7 days
▪︎no single effective tx; goals: maintain good oral hygiene, avoid exacerbating factors, + ⇣pain
▪︎soft bristle toothbrush + gently floss daily to avoid excessive trauma; wax over the abrasive points of braces
▪︎nonalcohol mouthwash; avoid sodium lauryl sulfate-containing toothpaste; avoid foods that seem to exacerbate sx
: S. viridans, H. influenzae, S. pneumoniae, S. pyogenes
: obstruct (ex, stones), dehydration, immune disorders, advanced age, malnutrition
▪︎⇡risk: older postop pts · poor oral hygiene · prematurity/low birth wt
acute onset unilat, painful swelling & erythema overlying salivary gland
▪︎firm swelling from the preauricular area to the angle of the mandible (d/c from the Stensen duct)
▪︎d/c from Stensen duct: gram stain + cx
▪︎admit for hydration + IV abx — infection can spread to deep fascial spaces (life-threatening)
▪︎empiric regimen varies: community- vs hospital-acquired (often hospital-acquired in older postop pts)
▪︎community-acquired: amp-sulbactam OR cefuroxime + metronidazole; nafcillin + (ceftriaxone or levofloxacin) or + (metronidazole or clindamycin)
▪︎hospital-acquired/IC: (vancomycin or linezolid) + cefepime + metronidazole, imipenem, meropenem, or pip-tazo
▪︎outpatient oral options: amox-clav OR clindamycin OR cephalosporin + metronidazole
▪︎complications: spread to deep fascial spaces (life-threatening) · resp obstruction · septic thrombophlebitis (Lemierre) · bacteremia · osteomyelitis
▪︎noninfectious: sialolithiasis, ETOH use d/o, DM, uremia, drugs (anticholinergics, antihistamines), malignancy
bilat parotid gland swelling w/o purulent d/c
▪︎HSV lesions: burning sensation → painful vesicles that break open + crust over
▪︎herpes lesions MC on the outside of the mouth (vs aphthous ulcers: oral mucosa)
▪︎herpes lesions are contagious; aphthous ulcers are ⍉
▪︎counsel pts to avoid oral sex until lesions completely resolve
▪︎triggers: stress, menstruation, UV sunlight, fever, lip trauma
▪︎prophylactic acyclovir or valacyclovir if ≥6 HSV outbreaks/yr
